name: Linguistics
notes: Ten courses: five core courses plus five electives, at least three of the electives at the 200 level or above.

Four of the five electives should fit a suggested track (Linguistic Theory; Language Documentation and Description; Language Variation and Change; Computational Linguistics; Language and the Mind) or an individualized track approved by the Director of Undergraduate Studies. The audit picker records a suggested track and fills four electives from that track's named courses; the fifth elective stays open. Individualized tracks are not a closed list — leave the picker unset and plan those electives with the DUS.
LING 214 Statistical Methods in Linguistics is recommended, not required.

requirementGroups.label: Core courses
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: All majors must take our five core courses: LING 110 Intro to Linguistic Analysis; LING 210(W) Intro to Language Sound Systems; LING 220 Intro to Syntax; LING 225 Intro to Semantic Analysis; LING 389 Senior Seminar

requirementGroups.label: Track electives (4 of 5)
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Students are encouraged to choose one of the 5 thematic tracks suggested below. Alternatively, students may propose a track organized around a different theme. Individualized tracks must be consulted with and approved by the Director of Undergraduate Studies. Four of the five electives must fit the track.
requirementGroups.note: Each suggested track has internal ALL-OF / ONE-OF structure; the planner asks for four courses from that track's named list. At least three of the five electives must still be 200-level — not auto-enforced here.

requirementGroups.label: Linguistics elective (1 more)
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Students must also take five additional electives, at least three of which must be at the 200-level or above.

upperLevelWriting.label: Upper-level writing within the major
upperLevelWriting.note: NEEDS VERIFICATION: the major page states no explicit upper-level-writing policy. Modeled as the College's two-course norm satisfied by the department's W-designated courses (LING 210W, 240W, 260W, 265W, 270W all exist in the catalog).
